endpoints.finding_headline: GET /members/{id}: the operation declares no security requirement, yet it returns the Member object including role and contactEmail. Anyone can read any member's record by guessing or enumerating the id.

GET /orders: the target member comes from the client-supplied required query parameter `memberId`. If the server does not compare it with the bearer's own member id, any authenticated user can list another member's orders (BOLA/IDOR).

POST /invoices: the body takes a client-supplied `orderId`. The spec does not show an ownership check, so a caller may be able to create invoices for orders that are not theirs. The documented 500 response also hints at unhandled errors, for example for an unknown orderId.

PUT /members/{id}/role: any holder of a memberToken may be able to set any member's role, including their own. The spec shows no admin or role requirement, and the body takes a free-form string `role`. This is a function-level authorization and privilege-escalation risk.
